Casting a string to int takes the leading numeric portion, so '42abc' becomes 42.
PHP converts the numeric string '5' to an integer for arithmetic, so 5 + 5 = 10.
In PHP, false cast to string becomes an empty string "", while true becomes "1".
Due to floating-point precision, 0.1 + 0.2 yields 0.30000000000000004, which is not strictly equal to 0.3.

str_contains checks if the haystack contains the needle 'world', which it does.
str_pad() can pad on the right, left, or both sides using the optional pad_type argument (STR_PAD_RIGHT, STR_PAD_LEFT, STR_PAD_BOTH).

Strings are immutable in PHP; ucfirst() returns a new string rather than modifying the argument in place.
Heredoc (<<<EOT) parses variables like double-quoted strings, while nowdoc (<<<'EOT') treats content literally with no interpolation.
sort() reindexes the array with numeric keys, so it does not preserve key-value associations (asort() does).
PHP automatically casts string keys that contain canonical decimal integers (like '5') to integer keys.
in_array() uses loose (==) comparison by default; strict comparison requires setting the third parameter to true.
Without a callback, array_filter() removes entries that are falsy when evaluated as boolean.
By default array_slice() reindexes numeric keys; you must pass true as the fourth parameter to preserve them.
array_slice takes 2 elements starting at offset 1, returning [20, 30].
The + union keeps left array's 'a' => 1 and adds 'b' => 2, giving 2 elements.
The spread operator in array literals still only supports integer-keyed (list-like) arrays; string keys cause an error.
Named arguments can be combined with argument unpacking in the same call, e.g. foo(...$args, named: 1).
Anonymous functions in PHP do not automatically inherit outer scope variables; they must be explicitly imported with use or via closures bound scope.
func_num_args() returns the actual number of arguments passed at call time, regardless of the declared parameter list.

A static closure cannot bind $this, so it does not capture the current object automatically.
use ($x) captures the variable by value at closure creation, so later changes don't affect it.
In weak (coercive) typing mode, the numeric string "5" is automatically coerced to int 5.
Constructor property promotion was introduced in PHP 8.0, allowing properties to be declared directly in constructor parameters.
Declaring a method as final prevents subclasses from overriding it.
The final keyword prevents a method from being overridden by child classes.
Private properties are only accessible within the class that declares them; subclasses cannot access them directly.
An anonymous class instance's class name begins with 'class@anonymous' followed by script path and position details.
Private parent methods are not inherited, so a child class may declare a method with the same name and any visibility without conflict.
__get() is called for inaccessible properties, including private/protected ones from outside their scope, not just non-existent ones.
Modifying a readonly property after initialization throws an instance of the Error class.
PHP interfaces can declare constants, which are inherited by implementing classes.
The instanceof operator checks whether an object is an instance of a class or interface.
Since PHP 5.3 (for static methods generally) interfaces may declare static methods, which implementing classes must define statically.
instanceof also returns true when the object implements a given interface, not just for class inheritance.
PHP interfaces only declare method signatures; default implementations are provided by traits, not interfaces.
Abstract methods can be declared public, protected, or private (private only within the same class hierarchy), so protected visibility is allowed.
cases() returns an array of all enum cases, which are A, B, and C.
Traits cannot declare constants; they may only define properties and methods.
Both Exception and Error implement the Throwable interface in PHP 7+.
TypeError extends Error, not Exception, so a catch (Exception $e) block will not catch it.
The @ operator only suppresses errors and warnings raised via PHP's error handling (diagnostics), not exceptions, which always propagate and must be caught.
intdiv() throws DivisionByZeroError (a subclass of ArithmeticError) when the divisor is zero.
The finally block runs regardless of whether an exception was thrown or caught.
An exception thrown in a finally block propagates and overrides any pending return value or exception from the try block.
Any object, including an Exception instance, casts to boolean true.
Shutdown functions run after script execution ends, including when exit() or die() is called.
The use statement only creates an alias; the class file is loaded by the autoloader when the class is actually used.
Namespaced function imports use 'use function', while 'use const' imports constants.
PSR-4 replaces the App\ prefix with src/, mapping the remaining namespace parts to directories.
Composer's generated autoloader registers its class loader(s) using spl_autoload_register().
The __NAMESPACE__ magic constant holds the name of the current namespace at compile time.

An unqualified class name is resolved relative to the current namespace (via __CLASS__ aliasing / import rules), not from the global root; only fully qualified names with a leading backslash refer to the global root.
PSR-4 replaces the namespace prefix 'App\' with 'src/', so App\Model\User maps to src/Model/User.php.
use statements are file-level (or namespace-level) declarations; they cannot appear inside a function and their effect is not limited to a function scope.
In PHP, assigning an array to another variable creates a copy (optimized with copy-on-write), unlike objects which are passed by handle.
PHP arrays are copied by value, so $b is a separate copy and appending 3 to it doesn't affect $a.

When foreach iterates by value, it operates on a copy of the array (since PHP 7 it avoids copying until modification, but the iteration is over the original snapshot), so modifications to the array inside the loop are not visible during the same pass.
A static property belongs to the class itself, so it is shared across all instances and changes are visible to every object.
PHP array keys are cast to integers or strings, so boolean true becomes the integer key 1.
Since PHP 7, a generator can return a value with return, retrievable via $gen->getReturn() after it finishes.
Once a generator has finished iterating, calling rewind() throws an Exception because generators cannot be rewound.
yield from delegates iteration to another generator, array, or Traversable object, yielding all its values.
A function containing yield returns a Generator object, so get_class returns 'Generator'.
The generator yields three elements, and iterator_to_array keeps them all.
SplStack is a LIFO stack; SplQueue implements FIFO.
ArrayIterator wraps an array or object so it can be iterated using the Iterator interface.
ArrayObject implements IteratorAggregate, so it can be traversed with foreach.
Since PHP 5.5, password_hash() automatically generates a cryptographically secure salt and embeds it in the resulting hash; the salt option is deprecated.
PASSWORD_DEFAULT in PHP 8 is bcrypt (password_hash handles salting automatically), and md5 is not a supported password algorithm.
password_verify correctly checks the plaintext against the hash, including its embedded random salt, so it returns true.
strip_tags() removes HTML tags from strings; SQL injection protection requires parameterized queries or escaping functions.
session_regenerate_id() replaces the session ID with a new one, preventing session fixation attacks after login.
php_sapi_name() returns a string with the name of the Server API, such as 'cli'.
session_destroy() removes server-side session data, but the session cookie remains in the browser until removed with setcookie() or expires.
$_SESSION is only populated after session_start() is called, since PHP must load the session data explicitly.

Asymmetric visibility (e.g., public private(set)) was introduced in PHP 8.4.
The #[\NoDiscard] attribute was introduced in PHP 8.5 to mark functions whose return values should not be ignored.
The pipe operator |> was accepted and introduced in PHP 8.5.

array_first() and array_last() were introduced in PHP 8.4.

The clamp_v2 RFC introduced the clamp() function, which was implemented for PHP 8.4.
The Context Managers RFC (based on Python-style 'with' using __invoke) is still under discussion and has not been adopted in PHP.
The generics RFC was declined by PHP internals, so bound-erased generic types are not part of PHP.
No RFC has been accepted to make multithreading (ZTS) the default in PHP; ZTS remains optional.
PHP 8.5 does not support generics; they remain a long-requested but unimplemented feature.

The PHP 6 project was abandoned and PHP 5.6 was followed directly by PHP 7.0.
The RFC to add the #[\Deprecated] attribute was accepted and implemented in PHP 8.4.
In clean and onion architecture, dependencies always point inward, with inner layers having no knowledge of outer layers.
Domain entities should be framework- and persistence-agnostic, depending only on PHP itself (and possibly the standard library).
Controllers and templates belong to the presentation/interface layer; they only trigger use cases, which themselves implement the business logic.
Onion architecture places the domain model at the core, with layers of domain services, application services, and infrastructure wrapping around it.
Tools like deptrac analyze dependencies between layers and automatically fail builds when forbidden calls or layer violations are detected.
A use case should be framework-agnostic and receive only plain values or its own abstractions, not HTTP requests or ORM objects like EntityManager.
A Repository provides a collection-like interface over aggregates/entities while encapsulating the storage mechanism.
In clean architecture, the domain and use case layers are independent of infrastructure details, so swapping the database only affects the outer layer.
An aggregate is a DDD concept: a cluster of domain objects treated as a single consistency unit with one root, not merely a database table.
Value Objects are immutable and equality is based on field values rather than object identity.
In Domain-Driven Design, the aggregate root is the single external entry point through which all changes to an aggregate must pass.
Repositories are defined per aggregate root, since only roots should be loaded and persisted directly.
In Domain-Driven Design, the ubiquitous language is a shared vocabulary used by both developers and domain experts, reflected directly in the model.
The context is the boundary within which a model and its language remain consistent, while outside it the same words may refer to different models.
DDD advocates rich domain models with behavior on the objects, not anemic models where logic lives in services.
In domain-driven design, each bounded context has its own model, so the same concept (e.g., Customer) is represented by separate classes in different contexts.
Symfony services are only instantiated when they are first requested from the container.
The Symfony console command `php bin/console debug:router` lists all registered routes.
Symfony autowiring automatically registers and injects services, so manual declaration is not required for every service.
Twig compiles each template into a PHP class that is cached on disk and reused across requests for performance.
In the dev environment Symfony tracks the container's resource files and only recompiles the DI container when one of them changes.
Symfony uses the APP_ENV environment variable to select the active environment (e.g. dev or prod).
Symfony controllers must be public methods to be invokable by the framework's routing.
Subscribers and listeners are ordered by priority (and registration order), not by which interface they implement.
Symfony 6.0 removed the Guard system, making authenticator-based authentication (AuthenticatorInterface) the standard.
The Symfony IsGranted attribute checks roles/permissions on a controller method and throws a 403 AccessDeniedException if not satisfied.
Symfony voters are the recommended mechanism for deciding access to specific objects via isGranted() with a subject like $post.
Since Symfony 7, doctrine/annotations support has been removed, so validation constraints must use PHP native attributes like #[Assert\NotBlank].
Symfony forms include CSRF protection by default, automatically adding and validating a token field on submission.
Client-side checks are only a convenience; Symfony always validates the submitted data on the server.
Symfony's `make:form` command (from MakerBundle) generates a FormType class.
Symfony's security system stores the session as a serialized token without the plain-text password (it only re-authenticates on login), so passwords are never kept in plain text in the session.
Symfony stores bundle configuration in config/packages, typically one file per bundle or topic.
This is the recommended practice (e.g., in Symfony): .env holds safe dev defaults committed to the repo, while real secrets go in .env.local which is git-ignored.
The `debug:container` command lists all registered services and their aliases in the service container.
The compiled container is frozen after the kernel boots, so calling setParameter() at runtime from a controller throws an exception.
Since Symfony 4, services are private by default (public: false) and can only be injected via constructor/method injection, not fetched directly from the container.
Bundles work with sensible defaults; configuration in config/packages is only needed to override or customize them.
In Symfony, environment variables are referenced in services.yaml with the %env(VAR)% syntax.
Symfony uses the APP_DEBUG environment variable (typically set to 1 or 0 in .env) to enable or disable debug mode, including the profiler and Twig debugging.
Symfony Messenger allows a message to be handled by multiple handlers; you can add several handlers tagged for the same message.
The sync transport processes the message immediately in the same process, bypassing the queue/worker entirely.
Symfony Messenger workers process queued messages via the messenger:consume console command.
In Symfony Messenger, the retry_strategy is configured individually per transport in the framework.messenger configuration.
Symfony Messenger's default serializer uses PHP's serialize() format (PhpSerializer), not JSON; JSON is only used if you configure the Symfony serializer transport.
The Symfony Scheduler component triggers scheduled messages and dispatches them through Messenger transports (typically the scheduler_default transport).
The Symfony Messenger 'doctrine' transport stores queued messages in database tables managed by Doctrine.
Symfony Messenger allows adding custom middleware to the stack at the beginning or end via the messenger.middleware configuration.
Symfony follows a schedule of major releases every two years and minor releases every six months, in May and November.
Symfony's latest major versions target PHP 8.2 as the minimum required version.
Symfony 7.0 removed support for docblock annotations, requiring PHP attributes instead for validation, routes, etc.
Symfony's AssetMapper component serves and versions JS/CSS assets directly using importmap.php, with no Node.js or webpack required.
Symfony 6.4 is an LTS release with extended support until November 2027.
Major Symfony releases remove features deprecated in the previous branch, so deprecations stop working.
Each Symfony major release includes an UPGRADE guide documenting the changes needed to migrate.
The Symfony AssetMapper component serves and versions assets and manages import maps without needing Node.js or Webpack.
Symfony 8.2 is scheduled for release at the end of November 2026, after 2026-11-07.
Symfony follows a six-month release cycle, so after 8.0 (Nov 2025) and 8.1 (May 2026), Symfony 8.2 is scheduled for November 2026.
Symfony skips .3 and .4, so after the last 8.x minor (8.1 in this scenario) the next major 9.0 follows, mirroring the 6.4→7.0 pattern.
Symfony has no version 8.2, and even its actual releases follow backward-compatible minor releases where only major versions break APIs.
PHP maintains backward compatibility within a major version branch, so minor upgrades like 8.1 to 8.2 should not require code changes (aside from rare deprecations).
Following Symfony's release pattern (like 6.4 before 7.0), the last minor of the 8.x branch is 8.4.
Symfony 8.x requires PHP >= 8.4, not PHP 8.5, so upgrading PHP to 8.5 would not be mandatory.
Symfony guarantees that deprecations remain in place until the next major version, so 8.x deprecations are only removed in 9.0.
Twig templates cannot call arbitrary PHP functions directly; only whitelisted functions/filters are available.
Twig enables auto-escaping (as HTML) by default for templates, so printed variables are escaped automatically.
The |e filter escapes a string for safe output, defaulting to the HTML context (|e('html')).
The format_number filter from twig/intl-extra formats a number according to a given locale using ICU rules.
The |raw filter marks a value as safe, so Twig does not auto-escape it.
In Twig, {{ }} outputs expression values and {% %} executes logic tags like if, for, and set.
Twig allows declaring variables in templates with the {% set %} tag.
The dump() function outputs the debug information of a variable when Twig debug mode is enabled.
Bootstrap provides ready-made CSS/JS UI components and is not a single-page application framework like React or Vue.
The .container class is responsive with a fixed max-width at each breakpoint, unlike .container-fluid which is full width.
The Bootstrap grid uses 12 columns, not 16.
Bootstrap has six named breakpoints (sm, md, lg, xl, xxl) since the extra-small case uses no infix, so the listed infixes total five but Bootstrap's breakpoint system includes six tiers overall.
In Bootstrap, spacing utilities like .mt-3 multiply the base $spacer variable (1rem) by the given number.
In Bootstrap 5, interactive components are initialized via data-bs-toggle, e.g. data-bs-toggle="dropdown".
Bootstrap 5 removed the jQuery dependency and its components are written in vanilla JavaScript.
Dark mode in Bootstrap 5.3 is enabled with the data-bs-theme="dark" attribute, not a .dark class.
Doctrine does not auto-create tables at runtime; schema must be created explicitly with migration or schema tools.
EntityManager::persist() schedules a new entity for management, deferring SQL execution until flush() is called.
Doctrine ORM 3 removed EntityManager::merge(), so it no longer exists and cannot make an object managed.
DQL (Doctrine Query Language) operates on entities, associations, and their fields, which Doctrine translates into SQL on tables and columns.
Doctrine's find() returns null when no entity matches the given id.
DoctrineBundle does not automatically call flush(); you must call it explicitly, though Doctrine does automatically close/rollback the transaction on unflushed changes at shutdown.
Managed entities are tracked by the Unit of Work, so changed properties are persisted on flush() without calling persist() again.
remove() only schedules the entity for deletion; the DELETE query is executed when flush() is called.
MVCC in PostgreSQL allows readers not to block writers and writers not to block readers.
The EXPLAIN statement shows how MySQL would execute a query without actually running it.

SERIAL is legacy shorthand that creates a sequence and sets a column default, while GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY is the SQL-standard mechanism with stricter semantics (e.g., the column is NOT NULL and its sequence can't be dropped independently).
PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct, so a UNIQUE constraint allows multiple rows with NULL by default.
PostgreSQL's string_agg(value, separator) aggregates strings into one with a delimiter.
Plain VACUUM reclaims dead tuple space for reuse within the table's files but does not return space to the operating system; only VACUUM FULL does.
The PARTITION BY clause in an OVER() definition splits rows into groups over which the window function is computed.
READ COMMITTED only prevents dirty reads; non-repeatable reads can still occur because each query sees the latest committed data.
Without an explicit BEGIN, PostgreSQL executes each statement in its own implicit transaction and commits it immediately (autocommit).
The COMMIT command ends a transaction and permanently saves all its changes.
Indexes help UPDATE and DELETE find matching rows quickly, just like SELECT.
PostgreSQL supports SAVEPOINT to roll back part of a transaction without aborting the whole transaction.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually executes the query to show real timing and row counts; plain EXPLAIN only shows the plan without running it.
pgvector is the PostgreSQL extension that provides vector types and index support (e.g., HNSW, IVFFlat) for similarity/embedding search.
A partial index only includes rows that satisfy its WHERE condition, indexing a subset of the table.
PostgreSQL implements SERIALIZABLE using Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI), which relies on predicate-based conflict detection rather than locking the rows read.
HTTP 201 means 'Created' — the request succeeded and a new resource was created.
HTTP 204 No Content indicates a successful request with no response body, commonly returned after a DELETE.
DELETE is idempotent by HTTP semantics—repeating it on the same resource yields the same end state (the resource remains deleted).
Access-Control-Allow-Origin is sent by the server in its response to tell the client which origins are permitted.
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests indicates the client has sent too many requests in a given time, i.e., exceeded a rate limit.
It's reversed: 4xx codes indicate client errors and 5xx codes indicate server-side errors.
The Content-Type header describes the MIME type of the body in HTTP requests and responses.
RFC 5789 defines PATCH as not required to be idempotent, while PUT must be idempotent.
You should use a timing-safe comparison like password_verify() or hash_equals() to avoid timing attacks.
CSRF tokens are generated server-side, stored in the session, and validated on the server for unsafe requests like POST.
CSP is delivered via the Content-Security-Policy HTTP response header.
OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework for granting access to resources; identity is handled by authentication protocols like OpenID Connect.
XSS is prevented by escaping output (e.g., htmlspecialchars) when rendering data, not merely by validating input before storing it.
The authorization server returns an authorization code to the redirect_uri, which the client exchanges for an access token.
Refresh tokens have a longer lifetime and are used to request new access tokens without re-authentication.
Salts don't need to be secret; they are typically stored alongside the hash and verification only requires them to be unique.
Test classes must extend PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase for PHPUnit to recognize and run their test methods.
setUp() runs before each test method; setUpBeforeClass() runs once before all tests.
A data provider supplies multiple argument sets, so the test runs once per set.
PHPUnit's expectException() method sets the expected exception class for a test.
It's the opposite: mocks verify method calls, while stubs only return canned data.
PHPUnit 10 deprecated metadata annotations in favor of native PHP attributes like #[DataProvider].
PHPUnit supports dependencies with the @depends annotation.
PHPUnit's --order-by=random option randomizes test execution order.
